ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT regime: Articles L561-1 through L561-59, L561-2-1 and L561-2-2, L562-1 through L562-2-1, L574-1 through L574-7 and Articles R561-1 through R561-60-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Directive (EU) 2024/1624. UBO register: Article L561-2-2 and Articles R561-57 to R561-58 of the Monetary and Financial Code, introduced by Décret n°2016-1523 of 23 November 2016; restricted-access regime enacted by Décret n°2023-542 of 29 June 2023 following the CJEU joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20. Company registration and National Company Register (Registre National des Entreprises - RNE): Articles L123-1 et seq., L210-1 to L210-10 and L227-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code, implemented by Décret n°2021-1587 of 7 December 2021 and operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI). Sanctions and asset-freezing regime: Articles L562-1 to L562-2-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code, EU Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) 833/2014, plus UN Security Council resolutions implemented by Commission decisions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II — Art. L. 210-1 et seq. (general formation rules), Art. L. 227-1 to L. 227-32 (société par actions simplifiée), Art. R. 123-31 et seq. (RCS registration) and Annex 1-1 (M0 form); Décret n° 2021-1489 (Guichet unique operated by INPI); Code des impositions sur les biens et services (alcohol excise and warehousing rules).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the judicial district of the registered office, via the INPI-operated Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) filed with the M0 'Déclaration de constitution de société' on the INPI Guichet unique; official proof of incorporation is the K-bis extract and the BODACC publication notice.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS; the capital is freely fixed in the articles and must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be fully paid up upon subscription; in-kind contributions must be fully delivered at incorporation, supported by a commissaire aux apports report where any in-kind contribution exceeds €7,500 or the aggregate exceeds one-half of the capital. Subscription funds must be blocked on a dedicated bank account or in notarial consignation (de facto escrow) and are released only upon presentation of the K-bis registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE INCORPORATORS OF [COMPANY] Pursuant to Articles L. 227-1 and L. 227-9 of the French Commercial Code, the undersigned incorporators unanimously resolve: (1) The share capital of €10,000, comprising 1,000 ordinary shares of €10 each, is hereby subscribed, issued and fully paid up as stated in the subscription schedule. (2) The registered office is fixed at [Address], with jurisdiction and greffe publicity to follow. (3) [Name] is appointed President of the SAS with the fullest powers to act in all circumstances on behalf of the company. (4) The President is authorized to open the corporate bank account, file the M0 declaration, obtain the K-bis extract, and complete all social and fiscal formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the statuts (articles of association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders' meeting; a French civil-law notaire is mandatory only when an in-kind contribution of real property is made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct an avocat to draft the statuts in French, verifying the SAS form, corporate name, corporate object (ISIC 4632 craft-beer and beverage wholesale distribution), duration (maximum 99 years), registered office, share capital, share classes, share-transfer restrictions, President's powers and decision-making rules. Have each founder sign every page; private signature (sous seing privé) suffices absent real-property contributions; if real property is contributed, execute an authentic notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts in French signed by all shareholders
Statement of share subscription and contribution schedule
Power of attorney of the signatory, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe queries the statuts for missing or inconsistent clauses, amend the statuts by a founders' meeting resolution and re-file through the Guichet unique supporting-message function; the initial filing date is preserved for up to 15 days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), reporting to the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; corporate formalities are filed through the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises, and tax portal is impots.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: To operate as an SAS, the non-resident shareholder files an incorporation dossier with the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises. After INSEE assigns the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, the entity receives a French VAT identification number (TVA) from DGFiP upon approval of the registration. The file must contain notarized or certified articles of association, legal representative identification, registered-office acceptance from the premises owner, and proof of paid-up share capital. The VAT number is mandatory before invoicing in France, including any intra-EU acquisitions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a French SAS is a separate fiscally opaque taxpayer. It has no pass-through option and is chargeable to corporate income tax (25% standard rate) on worldwide profits, subject to treaty relief and participation-exemption rules. Territorial scope includes French-source profits and foreign-source profits for resident entities. No tax-exempt zone is applicable to this wholesale and export activity; the regime is the ordinary French corporate tax/VAT regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box or comparable fiscal classification election: legal form conclusively determines tax treatment. Eligible parent companies may elect the French fiscal-integration regime (intégration fiscale) for wholly-owned 95%+ subsidiaries, and may adopt simplified VAT reporting or monthly/quarterly instalments. There are no voluntary hybrid mismatch elections; anti-hybrid rules are mandatory under French law implementing ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For taxable supplies of goods the domestic small-business exemption (franchise en base) applies only below EUR 85,800 annual turnover; the service threshold is EUR 37,500. A French SAS is nevertheless required to register without delay for its first invoicing, regardless of threshold, because craft-beer distribution involves excise-liable alcoholic beverages and potential intra-EU sales; the EUR 10,000 annual intra-EU distance acquisition ceiling further triggers mandatory local VAT registration. Overseas sellers must appoint a VAT fiscal representative in France if they have no EU establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B domestic invoicing must be issued in dematerialised structured XML/UBL format through French-certified partner dematerialisation platforms (PDPs) and reported to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), which serves as DGFiP's central clearance gateway. Export invoices are subject to e-reporting of transaction data, not to a real-time digital stamping or per-invoice pre-clearance model. Data transmission deadlines are harmonised with French VAT return cycles, and penalties apply for missing or rejected invoice submissions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate applies to (i) direct exports of beer to non-EU destinations, provided the goods physically leave the Union and are evidenced by customs documentation; and (ii) intra-Community supplies to customers holding a valid EU VAT number, subject to filing of the EU recapitulative statement and correctness of the customer's VAT status. Services ancillary to such international sales (e.g., freight and insurance) may be zero-rated. The seller must be the legal exporter or ensure the export contract names it as supplier; the period allowed for collecting export proof is generally within 90 days from dispatch.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation in DELTA / near-EU transit document T1 where applicable)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing departure from French/EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit confirmation proving conversion/receipt of foreign currency
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and, where applicable, EUR.1 Movement Certificate for preferential origin claims
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French Customs may retrospectively restore VAT at 20% with monthly late-payment interest (0.20% per month) plus an automatic penalty when the exporter cannot substantiate zero-rating within the legal documentation period. The standard penalty for deliberate inaccuracy is 40% of the underdeclared VAT; qualified tax fraud involving organised falsification of export records attracts an 80% penalty and criminal prosecution, including fines and imprisonment. Recurring wrong claims may also lead to loss of the right to deduct input VAT and disqualification from simplified VAT reporting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks, jointly with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for prudential licensing and AML/CFT supervision; external financial relations are governed by the French Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF) and EU capital-movement provisions (Art. 63 TFEU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully and unconditionally convertible in France. Capital and current account transactions are liberalised for EU/OECD counterparties; no prior exchange-control authorisation is required for foreign equity injections, dividend remittances, import payments, or trade-related FX conversions. Profit repatriation is unrestricted, with only a standard withholding tax regime on dividends to non-EU treaty residents (reduced under an applicable Double Tax Treaty or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying 10%+ holding of at least 24 months). Restrictions apply exclusively to sanctioned jurisdictions (Russia, Iran, Belarus, Syria, North Korea, Cuba) and to cash movements exceeding €10,000, which must be declared to TRACFIN. Wholesale alcoholic-beverage activity in France is not subject to foreign-investment screening and requires no state licence beyond a customs activity declaration (registration professionnelle) and excise-duty registration with the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds in 1990 (Law No. 90-614). Exporters may hold foreign-currency proceeds indefinitely in authorised accounts, convert at market rates at any time, and use them freely for trade settlement or hedging. The only obligations are (i) beneficial-owner information attached to wire transfers under EU Regulation 2015/847, and (ii) statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France for any cross-border transaction above €12,500, which is executed automatically by the instructed bank. No conversion ratio or repatriation timeline applies to the craft-beer export business.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) + Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) + Operational Account
Multi-currency Operational Account (USD/EUR) + Cross-border Wire Hub

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for day-to-day operational treasury but Low-Medium for capital escrow and large trade wires. ACPR-licensed French EMIs (Qonto, Shine) and passported EEA EMIs (Revolut, N26) offer onboarding within 3–7 days, eIDAS video KYC, SEPA Instant, and multi-currency cards; however, EMIs are not 'credit institutions' under the CRR and therefore cannot open statutory capital-blocked accounts, issue import/commercial letters of credit, or extend working-capital facilities, and they impose volume caps insufficient for US hopped-cargo wires above €100k per single transaction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted; no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically before a French authority. The SAS president and any non-EU-resident beneficial owner must undergo video-identification (eIDAS-qualified digital identity) and a remote KYC interview with the bank's compliance desk; documents issued abroad require apostille and sworn French translation. For the capital-blocked account opened before RCS registration, the founding mandatary (or notary) must sign, but physical presence can be waived at the bank's discretion for EU-resident representatives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-owner opacity: foreign shareholders holding >25% through a trust, offshore holding company, or a jurisdiction on the FATF grey list — automatic refusal under Art. L561-5 CMF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration (Actuel-RC form) filed with the greffe du tribunal; full constitutional charter of each direct and ultimate shareholder; trust-registry extract if applicable; sworn attestation of the legal origin of funds; apostilled and translated notarised powers of attorney; tax-residence certificates of all natural-person UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds alert on the inbound capital injection (wire from a non-EU parent exceeding €15,000–€50,000 flagged for justification).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Originator's bank statement showing accumulated balance; audited or certified financial statements of the parent; signed share-subscription agreement (bulletin de souscription); board resolution approving the capital increase; proof of the blocking of funds by the notary or depositary bank; sworn translation of all non-French documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-screening hit or jurisdiction nexus: any trace to a sanctioned individual, entity, or country in EU Regulation 833/2014 or 2580/2001 lists; risks of refusal for cannabis-adjacent or counterfeit-brand exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions-screening report from an accredited provider; ownership-chain full transparency; customs IPA/EBDO registration for alcoholic-beverage wholesale; health and hygiene certificates (DGCCRF conformity); certificate of origin and excise-duty compliance statements for each beer consignment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity new-account activity: brand-new SAS requesting multiple six-figure cross-border wires and direct-debit collections within the first 30 days of opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 12-month treasury plan; signed commercial contracts with brewery suppliers and wholesale buyers (3 purchase orders min.); proforma invoices and the cold-chain logistics schedule; proof of EORI/RCS/VAT registration; list of counterparties with their own KYB dossiers; irrevocable undertaking that no cash deposits will be made.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a French SAS in formation, cash contributions must be deposited either with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or into a blocked account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the company in formation at a Tier-1 French bank (Art. R.227-1 Code de commerce). The non-EU parent investor wires via SWIFT MT103 with clear originator information (name, address, account) and purpose text 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – APPORT EN CAPITAL'; the bank maps it to the Banque de France balance-of-payments motif for inward direct investment in resident-equity capital and automatically reports the flow if it exceeds €12,500. Upon registration at the RCS and issuance of the Kbis, the notary's or depositary bank's attestation releases the block into the operational account. KYC evidence required: UBO declaration, share-subscription schedules, proof of identity of the legal representative, and tax-residence certificates; the transfer must be denominated in EUR and must originate from the shareholder's own account, not a third-party consolidated account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU and domestic supplier payments (hops, kegs, canning lines, cold-chain logistics) settle via SEPA Credit Transfer, with SEPA Instant for time-critical cold-chain invoices and SEPA Direct Debit (Core) for recurring B2B collections from wholesale buyers in France/Benelux. Non-EU imports (US malt, CTZ hops, equipment) route via SWIFT MT103 with ABA/IBAN routing and the customs-aligned BOP purpose code for general merchandise imports; larger procurement is secured by a documentary Letter of Credit (UCP600, confirmed or silent-confirmed at the exporter's risk) transmitted via SWIFT MT700/MT707. Excise duties and import VAT on beer are paid to DGDDI through the operational account using the DAA-CRDS online system, thereby avoiding customs-bonded interruption risks to the distribution pipeline.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forwards (tenor 1–24 months) under a French Master Agreement or ISDA/CSA with the relationship bank
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP plain-vanilla call/put options (premium-bearing) for downside protection on US malt and UK hop purchases
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EM currencies (e.g., BRL, TRY) limited to hedges against contingent emerging-market distributor sales, subject to bank's internal credit line
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR/USD) structuring term debt for stainless-steel keg fleets and cold-chain vehicles
Natural hedging via multi-currency accounts (EUR/USD/GBP) enabling full netting of trade receivables and payables without derivatives
FX spot aggregator/auto-trigger hedging (stop-loss and limit orders) executed on the bank's e-trading platform for tactical rebalancing of the USD seasonal working-capital cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential daily coercive penalty; directors may incur liability for failure to prepare or submit accounts. No automatic statutory strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts and related documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the Commercial Court through the Guichet unique or INPI filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine generally EUR 1,500, increasing to EUR 3,000 for repeat infringement; court order and daily coercive penalty may apply. Prolonged non-compliance may lead to registry radiation after formal notice, but no fixed automatic annual strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second working day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally applies at 0.20% per month, together with a surcharge generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on the circumstances and tax authority procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the Commercial Court through the Guichet unique or INPI filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation is required; file on incorporation and within 30 days after any change in beneficial-owner information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, potential criminal penalties for inaccurate or omitted information, and possible registration or registry measures. No automatic annual strike-off rule applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly under the normal regime, or annually under the applicable simplified regime; exact electronic deadline is assigned by the tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally applies at 0.20% per month, with tax surcharges generally ranging from 5% to 80% depending on the breach and enforcement stage.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory appointment rules may apply to qualifying groups, controlled entities, or shareholder control relationships.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority rules; IFRS may be used in permitted circumstances but is not generally mandatory for an unlisted SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual beneficial-owner confirmation. The SAS must maintain current beneficial-owner information and file an amendment within 30 days after any change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must be recorded in the shareholders' individual accounts and the register of movements of securities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholders' individual accounts and register of movements of securities
Register or records of corporate officers and legal representatives
Minute Book and signed shareholder and management resolutions
Annual accounts, management reports where applicable, and statutory auditor reports where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 540-2,160 per year, depending on provider, location, mail handling, and administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,160-8,640 per year for a small or medium-sized SAS, subject to transaction volume, consolidation, inventory, group reporting, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% rate on first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; R&D tax credit (up to 30% of eligible R&D expenditures); accelerated depreciation and other targeted deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200 - Corporate Tax Return (Déclaration de résultat) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr or Espace Entreprise portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15 May following the fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 May for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover excluding VAT and other operating revenues
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income; non-residents must declare worldwide income if a permanent establishment exists or specific French-source income applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before corporate tax after all allowable deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for transfer pricing adjustments and arm's length principle compliance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: €40 per month of delay up to a maximum of three months; additional 0.5% of the tax due per month late capped at 25% of the tax due; potential criminal prosecution for willful evasion with fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% flat-rate withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate from home-country tax authorities; submit DTA relief application with supporting documentation via impots.gouv.fr portal
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 15% depending on DTA (standard 12.8%); Interest: 0% to 15% depending on DTA (standard 12.8% for most cases)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million annual turnover for Local File; €750 million group turnover for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regime; compliance is governed by the arm's length principle under OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and Article 57 of the French General Tax Code, together with general anti-avoidance rules

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate non-declaration of taxable income or submission of false statements in tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to five years; civil restitution of evaded taxes plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, fines, and imprisonment; corporate veil may be pierced in cases of abuse of law

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining a company without economic substance solely for tax purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €500,000; potential dissolution of the entity; back taxes and penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for fines and may face imprisonment for fraudulent management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 5% to 10% of the adjustment amount; potential criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the tax adjustment and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering reporting or KYC requirements in cross-border transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or more; criminal penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability including fines and possible disqualification from management roles
